request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Deterministic rule-based insights over existing data (mortality threshold, low stock, lot expiry, overdue tasks/invoices, medicine withdrawal, breeding due/overdue, cycle past expected end). Each has `severity`, `title`, `message`, `why` (the rule and numbers behind it) and a `subject`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The "Alerts & insights" list.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Query filters: `severity`, `limit`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Query: `severity` (`critical`|`warning`|`info`), `limit` (1-50). `meta` has `total`, `by_severity`, `today`, `timezone`.
- No AI, scoring or stored state: the same data gives the same insight. Never returns 403: viewers see only rules their permissions allow.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Boolean query values: send `1`/`0` (`true`/`false` is rejected on most endpoints).

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — Sanctum session cookie. The user must be verified, onboarded and an ACTIVE member of the current farm (oldest active membership, or `X-Farm-Id`).

**ACCESS**
Any active farm member (no specific permission). The response is filtered by the caller's own permissions.

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/insights`

**QUERY PARAMETERS** (all optional unless marked required; booleans as `1`/`0`)
- `severity` — enum. Values: `critical`, `warning`, `info`
- `limit` — integer, min 1, max 50. Most insights to return, 1-50 (default 50).

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Query: `severity` (`critical`|`warning`|`info`), `limit` (1-50). `meta` has `total`, `by_severity`, `today`, `timezone`.
- No AI, scoring or stored state: the same data gives the same insight. Never returns 403: viewers see only rules their permissions allow.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` is an array of objects with fields: `id`, `code`, `severity`, `title`, `message`, `why`, `subject`, `data`.

`meta`: `total`, `by_severity`, `today`, `timezone`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403` — other codes: `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`, `onboarding_required`, `no_active_farm`, `farm_access_denied`.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
The report catalogue for this farm and viewer. A report whose data the viewer cannot see is NOT listed. Each entry has `filters` it accepts, `relevant` (false when the farm has no operation of that kind), `available`/`unavailable_reason`/`required_feature` (advanced reports need the `advanced_reports` plan feature), `exportable` and `export_formats`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The reports menu (only reports the user may run).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `report.view` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Run a report.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

---

**WHAT IT DOES**
Queues a CSV, XLSX or PDF export of a report. The work runs on the database queue, so the response is `202` with `status: "queued"`; poll the export (or watch for the `export_ready` / `export_failed` notification) and download when `completed`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Export" button on a report.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Required body fields: `report`, `format`, `idempotency_key`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `report.export` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates an export row and queues a job that writes a private file (retained 7 days).
- Omitted dates are defaulted when the request is made and the RESOLVED filters are stored and echoed back, so the file always matches the request.
- `idempotency_key` (8-80 chars) is required and unique per user and farm: the same key + same content returns the SAME export (`200`, "Export already requested."); the same key with a different report, format or filters is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Poll the export status.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Do not poll tightly: back off (e.g. 2s, 5s, 10s) or use the notification.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — Sanctum session cookie. The user must be verified, onboarded and an ACTIVE member of the current farm (oldest active membership, or `X-Farm-Id`). State-changing: needs the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script adds both).

**ACCESS**
Required backend farm permission: **`report.export`** — granted to: `owner`, `manager`, `finance`, `vet`. (Documentation only: the request never contains a permission string.)
Rate limited by limiter `report-export`: 20 per hour per user (configurable) (`429 too_many_requests` + `Retry-After`).

**URL**
`POST {{base_url}}/reports/exports`

**REQUEST BODY** (`application/json`)
- `report` — string, **required**, max 40 chars. A report code from GET /reports.
- `format` — enum, **required**. Values: `csv`, `xlsx`, `pdf`
- `filters` — object, optional. The same filters the report accepts. Omitted dates are defaulted when the export is requested, and the resolved filters are stored on the export.
- `filters.from` — string (date), optional
- `filters.to` — string (date), optional
- `filters.as_of` — string (date), optional
- `filters.production_cycle_id` — string (uuid), optional
- `filters.kind` — enum, optional. Values: `livestock`, `crop`
- `filters.status` — enum, optional. Values: `active`, `closed`, `completed`, `cancelled`
- `idempotency_key` — string, **required**, max 80 chars, min 8 chars. Required. Retrying the same request returns the same export; reusing the key with different content is a 409.

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Requires `report.export` + the report's data permissions + the plan feature `data_export` (`403 feature_not_available` otherwise).
- Omitted dates are defaulted when the request is made and the RESOLVED filters are stored and echoed back, so the file always matches the request.
- `idempotency_key` (8-80 chars) is required and unique per user and farm: the same key + same content returns the SAME export (`200`, "Export already requested."); the same key with a different report, format or filters is `409 idempotency_conflict`.
- Rate limited (20 per hour by default).
- Formats: `csv` (UTF-8 with BOM; spreadsheet-executable prefixes are neutralised), `xlsx`, `pdf` (landscape A4).

**SUCCESS**
`202 Accepted` — message: "Export queued."

`data` fields: `id`, `report`, `format`, `filters`, `status`, `row_count`, `file_name`, `file_size`, `download_path`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `requested_at`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `failed_at`, `expires_at`, `download_count`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403` — `forbidden` when the caller lacks `report.export`; other codes: `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`, `onboarding_required`, `no_active_farm`, `farm_access_denied`.
- `409` — conflict with current state.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).
- `419 session_expired` — missing/expired CSRF token: call "Initialise CSRF cookie" and retry once.
- `429 too_many_requests` — honour `Retry-After`.

response.name: 202 Accepted — Export queued.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Streams the finished file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, private/no-store, nosniff).

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Download" on a completed export.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Path ids (UUIDv7): `{{report_export_id}}`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `report.export` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Audit-logs the download.
- `409 export_not_ready` (queued/processing), `409 export_failed`, `410 export_expired`, `403` when the CURRENT permissions or plan no longer allow it - access is re-checked on every download.
- Only the requesting user on the same farm can download; anyone else gets `404`. Rate limited (30/min).

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Route by the UUIDv7 `id`; any `reference` code (`BAT-2026-00001`, ...) is display-only.
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Fetch with credentials as a Blob (`responseType: "blob"`) and save it; the file path is never exposed.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — Sanctum session cookie. The user must be verified, onboarded and an ACTIVE member of the current farm (oldest active membership, or `X-Farm-Id`).

**ACCESS**
Required backend farm permission: **`report.export`** — granted to: `owner`, `manager`, `finance`, `vet`. (Documentation only: the request never contains a permission string.)
Rate limited by limiter `report-download`: 30 per minute per user (`429 too_many_requests` + `Retry-After`).

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/reports/exports/{{report_export_id}}/download`

**PATH PARAMETERS**
- `{{report_export_id}}` — UUID. Captured by "Request a report export" (19 — Reports & Exports) or from the list endpoint of this resource.

**VARIABLES USED**
- `{{report_export_id}}` — captured by "Request a report export"

**BUSINESS RULES**
- `409 export_not_ready` (queued/processing), `409 export_failed`, `410 export_expired`, `403` when the CURRENT permissions or plan no longer allow it - access is re-checked on every download.
- Only the requesting user on the same farm can download; anyone else gets `404`. Rate limited (30/min).

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

Non-JSON body (`text/csv; charset=UTF-8`).

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403` — `forbidden` when the caller lacks `report.export`; other codes: `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`, `onboarding_required`, `no_active_farm`, `farm_access_denied`.
- `404 not_found` — unknown id, or an id that belongs to another farm (never distinguishable).
- `409` — `export_not_ready`, `export_failed`.
- `410` — conflict with current state.
- `429 too_many_requests` — honour `Retry-After`.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
The caller's in-app notifications for the current farm, newest first. `meta.unread_count` is the total unread count (use it for the bell badge).

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The notification bell/center.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Query filters: `unread`, `type`, `severity`, `page`, `per_page`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Notifications are created by a background job (`notifications:generate`, hourly) - never by an API call. They follow three separate steps: condition -> decision (permission, preference, dedupe) -> record. They point at their source and never change it.
- Deduplication: critical/warning once per farm-local day, info once per week per user while the condition persists; one `export_ready` per export.
- Query: `unread` (`1`/`0`; the strings true/false are rejected here), `type`, `severity`, `page`, `per_page`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Boolean query values: send `1`/`0` (`true`/`false` is rejected on most endpoints).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Locally, run `php artisan notifications:generate` to create some, or complete an export to receive `export_ready`.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — Sanctum session cookie. The user must be verified, onboarded and an ACTIVE member of the current farm (oldest active membership, or `X-Farm-Id`).

**ACCESS**
Any active farm member (no specific permission). The response is filtered by the caller's own permissions.

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/notifications`

**QUERY PARAMETERS** (all optional unless marked required; booleans as `1`/`0`)
- `unread` — boolean. true = unread only, false = read only.
- `type` — string, max 40 chars
- `severity` — enum. Values: `critical`, `warning`, `info`
- `page` — integer, min 1
- `per_page` — integer, min 1, max 100

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Notifications are created by a background job (`notifications:generate`, hourly) - never by an API call. They follow three separate steps: condition -> decision (permission, preference, dedupe) -> record. They point at their source and never change it.
- Deduplication: critical/warning once per farm-local day, info once per week per user while the condition persists; one `export_ready` per export.
- Query: `unread` (`1`/`0`; the strings true/false are rejected here), `type`, `severity`, `page`, `per_page`.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` is an array of objects with fields: `id`, `type`, `severity`, `title`, `message`, `source`, `data`, `is_read`, `read_at`, `created_at`.

`meta`: `current_page`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `total`, `unread_count`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403` — other codes: `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`, `onboarding_required`, `no_active_farm`, `farm_access_denied`.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).

Any active farm member (no specific permission). The response is filtered by the caller's own permissions.

`POST {{base_url}}/notifications/{{notification_id}}/read`

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Who did what, when, to which resource: a newest-first timeline built IN PLACE from the authoritative append-only records, plus a small log of privileged actions (team, farm settings, exports).

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The audit log screen (owners/managers).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Query filters: `from`, `to`, `actor_id`, `action`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `request_id`, `production_cycle_id`, ....

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `audit.view` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Query: `from`, `to` (farm-local days on `performed_at`), `actor_id`, `action` (for example `record.created`, `sale.cancelled`, `team.invitation_sent`), `resource_type`, `resource_id` (everything that happened to one resource, including its reversals), `request_id` (the `X-Request-Id` of the causing request), `production_cycle_id`, `page`, `per_page` (max 100).
- `performed_at` = when it happened in the system; `recorded_at` = the business time of the event. Never merged.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Boolean query values: send `1`/`0` (`true`/`false` is rejected on most endpoints).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — Sanctum session cookie. The user must be verified, onboarded and an ACTIVE member of the current farm (oldest active membership, or `X-Farm-Id`).

**ACCESS**
Required backend farm permission: **`audit.view`** — granted to: `owner`, `manager`. (Documentation only: the request never contains a permission string.)

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/audit`

**QUERY PARAMETERS** (all optional unless marked required; booleans as `1`/`0`)
- `from` — string (date). Inclusive farm-local days, applied to when the action was performed.
- `to` — string (date)
- `actor_id` — string (uuid)
- `action` — string, max 60 chars. Exact action code, for example `record.reversed` or `team.member_role_changed`.
- `resource_type` — string, max 40 chars
- `resource_id` — string (uuid). Everything that happened to one resource (including the reversal/correction rows that point at it).
- `request_id` — string, max 100 chars
- `production_cycle_id` — string (uuid)
- `page` — integer, min 1
- `per_page` — integer, min 1, max 100

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Requires `audit.view` (Owner, Manager). A source is only included when the viewer may also view that module.
- Query: `from`, `to` (farm-local days on `performed_at`), `actor_id`, `action` (for example `record.created`, `sale.cancelled`, `team.invitation_sent`), `resource_type`, `resource_id` (everything that happened to one resource, including its reversals), `request_id` (the `X-Request-Id` of the causing request), `production_cycle_id`, `page`, `per_page` (max 100).
- `performed_at` = when it happened in the system; `recorded_at` = the business time of the event. Never merged.
- Never included: money amounts, record details/notes/reasons, tokens or secrets.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` is an array of objects with fields: `id`, `action`, `resource`, `actor`, `performed_at`, `recorded_at`, `changes`, `request_id`, `ip_address`, `related_id`, `production_cycle`.

`meta`: `current_page`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `total`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403` — `forbidden` when the caller lacks `audit.view`; other codes: `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`, `onboarding_required`, `no_active_farm`, `farm_access_denied`.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).

item.name: 25 — Marketplace offers & purchase intents
item.description: **Phase 24.** Controlled negotiation on Marketplace listings: buyer offers (strictly below the listed unit price, not below the platform floor, max 3 per listing, 48h expiry), "proceed at listed price" purchase intents, and the shop's accept/reject. Sign-in + verified email only (NO farm). NOT chat, escrow or checkout: nothing is reserved, paid or sold, and seller contact is never returned (Phase 25). Platform settings: `marketplace_max_offers_per_buyer`, `marketplace_offer_expiry_hours`, `marketplace_min_offer_percent` (folder 90 -> settings). Contract: `docs/api/PHASE-24-MARKETPLACE-OFFERS.md`. These requests were NOT executed with Newman (see COVERAGE).

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
A buyer proposes a unit price and quantity on a NEGOTIABLE, public listing. Not a chat, escrow or checkout: nothing is reserved, charged or sold, and no seller contact is returned.

**INPUTS**
- `quantity` (decimal string; the unit's precision, minimum order, declared availability)
- `unit_price` (naira per ONE unit, <=2 decimals): strictly below the listed unit price and at least `marketplace_min_offer_percent` (default 70%) of it. Exact decimal arithmetic on the unit price, not the order total.

**RULES**
All validation (422/403/404/409 listing_not_negotiable) happens BEFORE an attempt is used. One open offer at a time (`409 offer_pending`); at most `marketplace_max_offers_per_buyer` (3) per listing - pending, accepted, rejected and expired count, voided do not (`409 offer_limit_reached` with `details.max_attempts/attempts_used`); `409 offer_already_accepted`; shop members and the linked farm's owner get `403 cannot_negotiate_own_listing`. Expires after `marketplace_offer_expiry_hours` (48h).

**NEXT**
The seller accepts or rejects (shop folder offers). Poll `GET /my/offers/{id}`.

item.name: 26 — Marketplace deals & contact exchange
item.description: **Phase 25.** A lightweight deal summary. Two yeses: the BUYER confirms an offer the seller accepted, or the seller confirms a fixed-price purchase request and then the BUYER confirms the exact terms. Frozen product/unit/quantity/price/total and fulfilment terms; two-sided self-reported completion; cancellation; confidential reports (moderation is Phase 27); audited contact exchange (address only for pickup). Farmvest is NOT an escrow, payment processor or logistics provider: no payment, stock reservation, sale or delivery. Shop permissions `deal.view` (all roles) and `deal.respond` (owner, manager); platform setting `marketplace_deal_confirmation_hours` (72). Contract: `docs/api/PHASE-25-MARKETPLACE-DEALS.md`. The executable proof is **Flow 17** (folder 99); these reference requests were not run individually.

item.name: 90 — Platform Admin
item.description:
**Platform administration is NOT farm administration.** Access comes only from a `platform_admins` grant created by an operator (`php artisan platform:grant-admin <email> --role=admin|support`); being a farm Owner confers nothing here and a platform admin has no farm powers unless they also hold a farm membership. Roles: `admin` (read + write) and `support` (read only).

These routes have no farm context, no `X-Farm-Id` and no farm permissions. Log in as the platform admin account first (**01 — Authentication → Log in as the platform admin**); your cookie jar then holds the admin session.

Typical screens: the separate platform administration console (not part of the farm UI).

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Confirms the caller holds a platform role and returns it. Platform access is granted only by an operator via `php artisan platform:grant-admin` - never through this API and never by being a farm Owner.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Deciding whether to show the Platform Admin area.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Platform Admin read: needs a platform role (`admin` or `support`), not a farm role.
- `403 platform_admin_required` for everyone without a grant.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — signed-in, email-verified user holding a **platform role**. This is NOT a farm role.

**ACCESS**
Platform role **`admin` or `support`** (no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).
Farm roles (Owner, Manager, ...) confer nothing here.

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/platform-admin/me`

**BUSINESS RULES**
- `403 platform_admin_required` for everyone without a grant.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` fields: `user`, `role`, `can_write`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403 platform_admin_required` — no platform grant; `403 platform_write_forbidden` — read-only (`support`) role on a write endpoint; `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Suspends an account: every session of that user stops working and login is refused with `403 account_suspended`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Suspending an abusive or compromised account.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Path ids (UUIDv7): `{{user_chidi_id}}`.
- Required body fields: `reason`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `admin` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Sets the suspended state and a platform audit entry.
- Requires the platform `admin` role.
- The account is not deleted and its farm data is untouched.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Route by the UUIDv7 `id`; any `reference` code (`BAT-2026-00001`, ...) is display-only.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — signed-in, email-verified user holding a **platform role**. This is NOT a farm role. State-changing: needs the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script adds both).

**ACCESS**
Platform role **`admin`** only (`support` is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`; no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).
Farm roles (Owner, Manager, ...) confer nothing here.
Rate limited by limiter `platform-admin-write`: 60 per minute per user (`429 too_many_requests` + `Retry-After`).

**URL**
`POST {{base_url}}/platform-admin/users/{{user_chidi_id}}/suspend`

**PATH PARAMETERS**
- `{{user_chidi_id}}` — UUID. Captured by "Accept a farm invitation" (03 — Farms, Team & Access) or from the list endpoint of this resource.

**REQUEST BODY** (`application/json`)
- `reason` — string, **required**, max 500 chars, min 3 chars. Kept in the audit trail.

**VARIABLES USED**
- `{{user_chidi_id}}` — captured by "Accept a farm invitation"

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Requires the platform `admin` role.
- The account is not deleted and its farm data is untouched.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` fields: `id`, `name`, `email`, `email_verified`, `onboarded`, `status`, `suspended_at`, `platform_role`, `active_farms_count`, `created_at`, `providers`, `farms`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403 platform_admin_required` — no platform grant; `403 platform_write_forbidden` — read-only (`support`) role on a write endpoint; `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`.
- `404 not_found` — unknown id.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).
- `419 session_expired` — missing/expired CSRF token: call "Initialise CSRF cookie" and retry once.
- `429 too_many_requests` — honour `Retry-After`.

Lifts a suspension: the user can log in again and their existing memberships and farm data are exactly as they were. Reversible counterpart of "Suspend a user".

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Lifting a suspension.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Path ids (UUIDv7): `{{user_chidi_id}}`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `admin` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Clears the suspended state (audited).
- Requires the platform `admin` role.
- Requires the platform `admin` role. `409 not_suspended` if the account is not suspended.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Route by the UUIDv7 `id`; any `reference` code (`BAT-2026-00001`, ...) is display-only.

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — signed-in, email-verified user holding a **platform role**. This is NOT a farm role. State-changing: needs the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script adds both).

**ACCESS**
Platform role **`admin`** only (`support` is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`; no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).
Farm roles (Owner, Manager, ...) confer nothing here.
Rate limited by limiter `platform-admin-write`: 60 per minute per user (`429 too_many_requests` + `Retry-After`).

**URL**
`POST {{base_url}}/platform-admin/users/{{user_chidi_id}}/restore`

**PATH PARAMETERS**
- `{{user_chidi_id}}` — UUID. Captured by "Accept a farm invitation" (03 — Farms, Team & Access) or from the list endpoint of this resource.

**VARIABLES USED**
- `{{user_chidi_id}}` — captured by "Accept a farm invitation"

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Requires the platform `admin` role.
- Requires the platform `admin` role. `409 not_suspended` if the account is not suspended.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` fields: `id`, `name`, `email`, `email_verified`, `onboarded`, `status`, `suspended_at`, `platform_role`, `active_farms_count`, `created_at`, `providers`, `farms`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403 platform_admin_required` — no platform grant; `403 platform_write_forbidden` — read-only (`support`) role on a write endpoint; `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`.
- `404 not_found` — unknown id.
- `419 session_expired` — missing/expired CSRF token: call "Initialise CSRF cookie" and retry once.
- `429 too_many_requests` — honour `Retry-After`.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Creates a new plan that starts INACTIVE (`is_active: false`) and non-default; it grants nothing until you set prices/entitlements and activate it with PATCH. `slug` is the stable machine identifier (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Set prices and entitlements with the two PUT endpoints.

- Requires the platform `admin` role (a `support` role is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`). Writes are rate limited (60/min).
- `is_active` and `is_default` cannot be sent on create (`422`); activate later with `PATCH {is_active: true}`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

Platform role **`admin`** only (`support` is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`; no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).

**URL**
`POST {{base_url}}/platform-admin/plans`

**REQUEST BODY** (`application/json`)
- `slug` — string, **required**, max 64 chars, pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. Stable machine identity; cannot be changed later.
- `name` — string, **required**, max 150 chars
- `description` — string, optional, max 2000 chars, nullable
- `currency` — enum, optional. Fixed to NGN for now.. Values: `NGN`
- `is_public` — boolean, optional
- `sort_order` — integer, optional, min 0, max 100000

**BUSINESS RULES**

- `is_active` and `is_default` cannot be sent on create (`422`); activate later with `PATCH {is_active: true}`.

**SUCCESS**

`data` fields: `id`, `slug`, `name`, `description`, `currency`, `is_active`, `is_public`, `is_default`, `sort_order`, `subscribers_count`, `prices`, `features`, `limits`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Lists reference records of one KIND. Kinds: `operation-types`, `species`, `crop-types`, `breeds`, `varieties`, `reference-values`. Filters: `q`, `is_active`, `parent_id`, `category`, `list` (for reference-values: `planting_material_type`, `planting_unit_type`), `page`, `per_page`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The reference-data admin list.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Query filters: `q`, `is_active`, `parent_id`, `category`, `list`, `page`, `per_page`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Platform Admin read: needs a platform role (`admin` or `support`), not a farm role.
- Any platform role (`admin` or `support`) may read.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Needs the signed-in session cookie (send requests with credentials).
- Boolean query values: send `1`/`0` (`true`/`false` is rejected on most endpoints).

---
**REFERENCE (detail)**

**AUTHENTICATION**
**Required** — signed-in, email-verified user holding a **platform role**. This is NOT a farm role.

**ACCESS**
Platform role **`admin` or `support`** (no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).
Farm roles (Owner, Manager, ...) confer nothing here.

**URL**
`GET {{base_url}}/platform-admin/master/species`

**QUERY PARAMETERS** (all optional unless marked required; booleans as `1`/`0`)
- `q` — string, max 100 chars. Matches name or code.
- `is_active` — boolean
- `parent_id` — string (uuid). Filter by the parent record (operation type / species / crop type id).
- `category` — enum. Operation types only.. Values: `livestock`, `aquaculture`, `crop`
- `list` — enum. Reference values only.. Values: `planting_material_type`, `planting_unit_type`
- `page` — integer, min 1
- `per_page` — integer, min 1, max 100

**BUSINESS RULES**
- Any platform role (`admin` or `support`) may read.

**SUCCESS**
`200 OK`

`data` is an array of objects with fields: `id`, `code`, `name`, `livestock_group`, `operation_type`, `sort_order`, `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

`meta`: `current_page`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `total`.

**ERRORS**
- `401 unauthenticated` — no valid session: show the login screen.
- `403 platform_admin_required` — no platform grant; `403 platform_write_forbidden` — read-only (`support`) role on a write endpoint; `account_suspended`, `email_verification_required`.
- `404 not_found` — unknown id.
- `422 validation_failed` — `errors` is keyed by field (nested keys like `details.quantity`); some domain rules return a specific `code` (for example measurement errors).

response.name: 200 OK

Platform role **`admin`** only (`support` is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`; no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`).

**WHAT IT DOES** Creates a DRAFT platform work template (visible to farms only after publishing). Same item model as farm templates plus a stable `code` (lowercase snake case). **WHEN TO USE IT** "New platform template" (draft). **IMPORTANT INPUTS** - Required body fields: `name`, `applies_to`, `items`, `code`. **IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR** - Requires the farm permission `admin` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client). - Audit entry. - Requires the platform `admin` role (a `support` role is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`). Writes are rate limited (60/min). - Template content is configuration, not veterinary or agronomic advice. **FRONTEND NOTES** - Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first). --- **REFERENCE (detail)** **AUTHENTICATION** **Required** — signed-in, email-verified user holding a **platform role**. This is NOT a farm role. State-changing: needs the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script adds both). **ACCESS** Platform role **`admin`** only (`support` is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`; no grant: `403 platform_admin_required`). Farm roles (Owner, Manager, ...) confer nothing here. Rate limited by limiter `platform-admin-write`: 60 per minute per user (`429 too_many_requests` + `Retry-After`). **URL** `POST {{base_url}}/platform-admin/work-templates` **REQUEST BODY** (`application/json`) - `name` — string, **required**, max 150 chars - `description` — string, optional, max 2000 chars, nullable - `applies_to` — enum, **required**. Values: `production_cycle`, `breeding_project` - `cycle_kind` — any, optional - `operation_type_id` — string (uuid), optional, nullable - `species_id` — string (uuid), optional, nullable - `crop_type_id` — string (uuid), optional, nullable - `breeding_workflow` — any, optional - `items` — array, **required**, min 1 items, max 50 items - `items[].anchor` — enum, **required**. The date a template item's offset_days counts from. | | |---| | `cycle_start`
| | `cycle_expected_end`
| | `breeding_start`
| | `breeding_expected`
Exact expected date, or the start of the expected window. | | `breeding_expected_to`
End of the expected window (falls back to the exact date). |. Values: `cycle_start`, `cycle_expected_end`, `breeding_start`, `breeding_expected`, `breeding_expected_to` - `items[].offset_days` — integer, optional, min 0, max 3650. Days after the anchor date of the first task. - `items[].until_offset_days` — integer, optional, min 0, max 3650, nullable. Recurring items: last day, as days after the anchor. - `items[].title` — string, **required**, max 200 chars - `items[].category` — enum, **required**. Closed task vocabulary served by GET /master/task-categories. . Values: `feeding_watering`, `egg_collection`, `vaccination_medication`, `breeding_reproduction`, `growth_monitoring`, `record_keeping`, `maintenance_repair`, `cleaning_sanitation`, `movement_rotation`, `procurement_orders`, `irrigation`, `crop_care`, `harvest`, `payment`, `other` - `items[].instructions` — string, optional, max 5000 chars, nullable - `items[].due_time` — string, optional, nullable - `items[].reminder_offsets` — array, optional, max 5 items, nullable - `items[].linked_record_type` — enum, optional, nullable. Values: `feed_use`, `egg_collection`, `milk`, `mortality`, `weight`, `temperature`, `water`, `irrigation`, `weeding`, `fertilizer_application`, `pesticide_application`, `land_preparation`, `planting`, `establishment_check`, `growth_stage`, `crop_loss`, `crop_harvest`, `pest_observation`, `general_note`, `population_adjustment`, `health`, `breeding_check`, `breeding_outcome`, `null` - `items[].requires_evidence` — boolean, optional - `items[].assigned_role` — any, optional - `items[].recurrence` — enum, optional. none = a single task; daily = every N days; weekly = every N weeks on the chosen ISO weekdays. . Values: `none`, `daily`, `weekly` - `items[].interval_value` — integer, optional, min 1, max 52 - `items[].weekdays` — array, optional, min 1 items, max 7 items, nullable - `items[].occurrence_limit` — integer, optional, min 1, max 3650, nullable - `code` — string, **required**, max 60 chars, pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` Server-owned fields — NOT accepted, sending any of them is a `422`: `is_active`. **VARIABLES USED** - `{{species_chicken_id}}` — captured by "List species" **BUSINESS RULES** - Requires the platform `admin` role (a `support` role is read-only: `403 platform_write_forbidden`). item.description:
Executable, end-to-end flows built from the same requests as the reference folders. **Run them in order** with the Collection Runner on the **Farm Management — Local** environment (each flow lists its prerequisites in its first request). Variables captured by earlier flows (`cycle_id`, `store_id`, ...) are reused by later ones. Every flow here was executed against the real application to produce the saved examples.

See `docs/postman/WORKFLOWS.md` for the state changes and business rules of each flow.

item.name: Flow 1 — Email registration & onboarding

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
PREREQUISITES: None (start of a fresh environment).

Sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie. Re-run it whenever a request fails with 419.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Initialises the CSRF cookie used by Laravel Sanctum cookie-based SPA authentication: the response is an empty `204` whose only job is to set the `XSRF-TOKEN` (readable) and session (HttpOnly) cookies. Every later POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE must echo the token in `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Once when the SPA boots, and again after any `419 session_expired`, before the first POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE from the SPA must echo the cookie value in the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header (URL-decoded). Axios does this automatically with `withCredentials: true` and `withXSRFToken: true`. The Postman collection does it for you in its collection-level pre-request script.
- The request must carry an `Origin` header that appears in `SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS` (the collection sends `{{frontend_origin}}`), otherwise the API treats the call as non-stateful and no session exists.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Register with email and password**.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **01 — Authentication** -> "Initialise CSRF cookie".

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
Creates the UNVERIFIED account and logs the user in. `next_action` is `verify_email`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Creates an UNVERIFIED account, starts the browser session (cookie) immediately and emails a 6-digit verification code. The response is the standard auth state with `next_action: "verify_email"`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The "Create account" form (email + password).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Creates the user, logs them in, sends an OTP email (locally: written to `storage/logs/laravel.log` when `MAIL_MAILER=log`). No farm is created.
- The user is logged in right after registration but is restricted: every farm-management endpoint answers `403 email_verification_required` until the code is verified.
- Password rules: 8-72 characters with at least one letter and one number; `password_confirmation` must match.
- Email is normalised (trimmed, lower-cased). A duplicate email is `422` on `email`.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Verify email with OTP**.

**FARM DISCOVERY (GAP-07)**
`data.farms` lists every farm the user ACTIVELY belongs to (`id`, `name`, `role`; oldest membership first). `data.farm` stays the default farm (the oldest active membership). To work in another farm send its `farms[].id` as the `X-Farm-Id` header, then refetch `GET /farm` (membership + permissions) and `GET /subscription/entitlements` and clear farm-scoped caches. There is no switch endpoint. Permissions are never listed here.

**MARKETPLACE-ONLY SELLERS (Phase 22)**
`data.marketplace.shop_count` = Marketplace shops the user belongs to (any status). `next_action = "marketplace"` is returned only for a verified user with NO active farm who belongs to at least one shop: route to the seller dashboard (`GET /marketplace/my/shops`). A brand-new account with no shop still gets `complete_farm_setup` (offer "open a shop instead" -> `POST /marketplace/shops`, no farm needed). A user with a farm keeps `none`. Farm endpoints still answer `403 onboarding_required` / `no_active_farm`; `POST /onboarding/farm` remains available.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Route on `data.next_action`, never on HTTP status alone. Registration needs the CSRF cookie and a stateful Origin first, otherwise `400 stateful_request_required`.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **01 — Authentication** -> "Register with email and password".

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
Route on `next_action`: `complete_farm_setup` -> show the farm-name screen.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The single request the frontend makes on every app load to decide where the user belongs: login, verify-email, farm setup, "no farm" screen or the application. Returns the same auth-state object as login/register.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
App load and after any auth change; the router reads `next_action` from it.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- `401 unauthenticated` means there is no session: show the login screen.
- `data.next_action` is one of `verify_email`, `complete_farm_setup`, `no_active_farm`, `none`.
- `data.farm` is the DEFAULT active farm (oldest active membership) with the caller's role. It does NOT list permissions - call `GET /farm` for `membership.permissions`.

**IN THIS FLOW**
A brand-new farm shows `kpis: []` and an `empty_state` with suggested actions.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The whole command centre for THIS farm and THIS viewer, in one call: `farm` (with `today` and `timezone`), `viewer`, `operations`, `sections`, `priority` insights, `kpis`, `work`, `calendar` strip, `quick_record`, `production`, `insights`, `recent_activity`, `quick_add` and an `empty_state`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The home screen; refetch after ledger-affecting actions.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Cards depend on the farm's operations and on what the viewer may see; a crop-only farm gets no population or egg cards.
- It is a READ MODEL: nothing is stored; every figure is read live from the owning module and reversed/cancelled events never count.
- Every block is gated by the viewer's own permissions, not by role names: a Farm Worker never receives money cards. `sections` says which blocks the viewer may see. The endpoint never returns 403.
- Operation-aware: a crop-only farm gets no population or egg cards. A brand-new farm gets `kpis: []` and an `empty_state` with suggested actions.

**ROUTE FORMS (GAP-06)**
`quick_add[].endpoint` is the absolute `/api/v1/...` URL (unchanged); `quick_add[].url` repeats it and `quick_add[].path` is the same route relative to `{{base_url}}`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Render cards from `kpis` generically (code/label/value/unit) and refetch after any ledger-affecting action.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
PREREQUISITES: Flow 1 completed (the account exists and is onboarded).



**WHAT IT DOES**
Initialises the CSRF cookie used by Laravel Sanctum cookie-based SPA authentication: the response is an empty `204` whose only job is to set the `XSRF-TOKEN` (readable) and session (HttpOnly) cookies. Every later POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE must echo the token in `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Once when the SPA boots, and again after any `419 session_expired`, before the first POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE from the SPA must echo the cookie value in the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header (URL-decoded). Axios does this automatically with `withCredentials: true` and `withXSRFToken: true`. The Postman collection does it for you in its collection-level pre-request script.
- The request must carry an `Origin` header that appears in `SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS` (the collection sends `{{frontend_origin}}`), otherwise the API treats the call as non-stateful and no session exists.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Log out**.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **01 — Authentication** -> "Initialise CSRF cookie".

Same as "Get current farm" but naming the farm explicitly with the optional `X-Farm-Id` header. The header selects among farms you actively belong to; it can never grant access (`403 farm_access_denied`).

Acting on a specific farm when a user belongs to several.

Take it from `GET /auth/me → data.farms[].id`. After switching, refetch `GET /farm`, `GET /subscription/entitlements` and clear farm-scoped caches.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
The command centre for this farm and viewer.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The whole command centre for THIS farm and THIS viewer, in one call: `farm` (with `today` and `timezone`), `viewer`, `operations`, `sections`, `priority` insights, `kpis`, `work`, `calendar` strip, `quick_record`, `production`, `insights`, `recent_activity`, `quick_add` and an `empty_state`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The home screen; refetch after ledger-affecting actions.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Cards depend on the farm's operations and on what the viewer may see; a crop-only farm gets no population or egg cards.
- It is a READ MODEL: nothing is stored; every figure is read live from the owning module and reversed/cancelled events never count.
- Every block is gated by the viewer's own permissions, not by role names: a Farm Worker never receives money cards. `sections` says which blocks the viewer may see. The endpoint never returns 403.
- Operation-aware: a crop-only farm gets no population or egg cards. A brand-new farm gets `kpis: []` and an `empty_state` with suggested actions.

**ROUTE FORMS (GAP-06)**
`quick_add[].endpoint` is the absolute `/api/v1/...` URL (unchanged); `quick_add[].url` repeats it and `quick_add[].path` is the same route relative to `{{base_url}}`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Render cards from `kpis` generically (code/label/value/unit) and refetch after any ledger-affecting action.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **18 — Dashboard & Insights** -> "Get the dashboard".

**IN THIS FLOW**
Switch the cookie session back to the farm owner.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Switches the session back to the farm owner.

**FARM DISCOVERY (GAP-07)**
`data.farms` lists every farm the user ACTIVELY belongs to (`id`, `name`, `role`; oldest membership first). `data.farm` stays the default farm (the oldest active membership). To work in another farm send its `farms[].id` as the `X-Farm-Id` header, then refetch `GET /farm` (membership + permissions) and `GET /subscription/entitlements` and clear farm-scoped caches. Farm endpoints still answer `403 onboarding_required` / `no_active_farm`; `POST /onboarding/farm` remains available.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
Captures `op_poultry_id` and `op_crops_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The production types the platform understands (Poultry, Cattle, Fishery, Crops, ...). Each carries `category` (`livestock`, `aquaculture`, `crop`) and `tracking_model` (`population` for livestock/fish heads, `planting_units` for crops). This is the first dropdown of "Start livestock batch / crop project".

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The first dropdown of "Start livestock batch / crop project" and the farm operations settings.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `operation`: Filter by operation code.
- `category`: livestock | aquaculture | crop
- `available`: `true` returns only operations usable by this farm.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `master_data.view` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Operations are optional preferences: when the farm has selected operations, `available=1` narrows the species/crop lists to them, but unfiltered lists still return everything and nothing is blocked. The dashboard also shows livestock or crop cards only when relevant to the farm.
- Never branch on `name`; use `code`, `category` and `tracking_model`.
- Every active operation is returned; `available` narrows to the farm's optional selection (see farm operations). `selected` = explicit farm choice.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **List species**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

**IN THIS FLOW**
Captures `species_chicken_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Species the farm can raise, optionally narrowed to one operation. Each item has `livestock_group`, `capability_codes` (the enabled behaviours) and a stable `code`. Fish is a species of the Fishery operation.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Species dropdown after an operation is chosen.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `master_data.view` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Which species appear can be narrowed by the farm's selected operations (`available=1`); the capability flags returned decide which record types and breeding workflows exist for that species.
- Filters: `operation` (operation code), `category`, `group` (`poultry`, `small_ruminants`, `large_ruminants`, `non_ruminant_mammals`, `equines`, `micro_livestock`), `available`, `include_inactive`.
- 21 livestock species plus fish ship by default; see docs/api/LIVESTOCK-CATALOGUE.md.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **List crops**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Fetch this list; do not hard-code species ids or names.

request.description:

**WHAT IT DOES**
A location is an optional site/building/field container ("Where is this?"). A farm starts with zero places and works without any.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Add location" in Farm → Places or inline in a form.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**

- `type` is one of `site`, `building`, `house`, `field`, `other`. `parent_id` (another location) is optional; nesting is limited to seven ancestors.
- Names are unique per kind + parent after trimming and case-folding, including inactive rows (`409 duplicate_location`).

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**

- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

request.description:
**WHAT IT DOES**
Receives a lot-tracked medicine: `lot {code, expires_on}` creates (or reuses) the lot. Expired lots cannot be used for treatment (`409 lot_expired`) but can be written off.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
Receiving medicine with a lot and expiry.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `recorded_at` = when it really happened (UTC, no milliseconds); `idempotency_key` = one UUID per user action.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `inventory.manage` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- One `stock_in` movement and a lot.
- Medicine items are normally lot-tracked: `lot {code, expires_on}` opens the lot (or joins the existing lot with the same code; a different expiry for an existing code is rejected).
- The quantity is in the item's unit dimension (`ml` here); packages resolve only through the item's own conversion.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**

- Derived numbers (population, stock, outstanding, totals) are authoritative on the server: refetch the affected resource and the dashboard after saving.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
`initial_population: 500` is the immutable baseline. Captures `cycle_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Starts a livestock batch (poultry, cattle, fish, ...): the production cycle that every livestock record, health event, breeding project, task and sale line later points at. The server assigns the UUIDv7 `id`, a readable `reference` such as `BAT-2026-00001` and `status: "active"`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The "Start livestock batch" form (poultry, cattle, fish, ...).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `production_cycle.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the cycle and its opening population movement. No inventory, finance or task side effects.
- `initial_population` is the immutable STARTING head count (fish are heads too). It is NOT the live population: `livestock.current_population` is derived from the population movement ledger (mortality, sales, births, adjustments) and can never be written directly.
- Counts must be positive whole numbers (JSON integers or digit strings). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar dates; historical dates are valid. Expected dates are optional user estimates and cannot precede the start.
- Name is unique per farm and kind, including closed cycles (`409 duplicate_cycle_name`).

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Show a production cycle**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Derived numbers (population, stock, outstanding, totals) are authoritative on the server: refetch the affected resource and the dashboard after saving.
- Build the form from master data: operation -> species -> breed. Show `current_population`, not `initial_population`, as "birds alive".

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **08 — Production Cycles** -> "Start a livestock batch".

**IN THIS FLOW**
Feed use documents what was fed; without an inventory link it moves no stock.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The same record type without an inventory link: it only documents the feed given. Use it when feed is not tracked as stock.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Record feed" on a batch without stock tracking.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `recorded_at` = when it really happened (UTC, no milliseconds); `idempotency_key` = one UUID per user action.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `record.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the record only. No inventory movement.
- A record says what DID happen. It is append-only: there is no PATCH or DELETE - correct with Reverse (and optionally a replacement using `corrects_record_id`).
- `recorded_at` is when the event really happened (UTC with seconds and `Z`/offset, no milliseconds, between the cycle start and now); the server keeps its own `created_at`.
- `idempotency_key` (1-80 chars of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, `-`) is required: same key + same payload returns the original record (201), changed payload is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**

- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
800 PLANTING UNITS (heaps) over 2 hectares. Captures `crop_cycle_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Starts a crop project. A crop project measures THREE separate things: land `area`, `initial_planting_units` (heaps/holes/stands) and later the planting-material quantity and harvest output. They are never converted into each other.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
The "Start crop project" form.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `production_cycle.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the cycle. No stock is deducted and no records are created.
- `initial_planting_units` is the baseline for establishment/survival checks. 800 heaps is not 800 tubers; seed/material quantity is recorded later by planting/input records and stock movements.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
12 bags + 18 kg = 318 kg. The balance is the sum of movements.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Appends a `stock_in` movement to the ledger. The item's balance is the sum of its movements - there is no balance column to edit. `components` are the entered parts (12 bags + 18 kg); they are normalised to the item's stock unit (12 x 25 kg + 18 kg = 318 kg).

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Receive stock" (opening balance, donation, manual intake).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `recorded_at` = when it really happened (UTC, no milliseconds); `idempotency_key` = one UUID per user action.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `inventory.manage` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- One `stock_in` inventory movement (and a lot if lot-tracked). No finance entry.
- Package units (bag, crate, bottle) resolve only through the item's own package conversion; otherwise `422 conversion_not_configured`.
- `reason`: `opening_balance`, `purchase`, `donation`, `other`. This endpoint creates NO supplier or expense; use Purchases for stock + expense together.
- Lot-tracked items need `lot_id` or `lot {code, expires_on}`. The location must be active with active ancestors.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **List inventory items with derived stock**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Unit codes come from `GET /master/units?dimension=...`; do not hard-code them.
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Derived numbers (population, stock, outstanding, totals) are authoritative on the server: refetch the affected resource and the dashboard after saving.
- Generate one idempotency key per user action (a UUID) and reuse it only when retrying that same action after a network failure.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **10 — Inventory** -> "Receive stock (stock-in)".

**WHAT IT DOES**

**IN THIS FLOW**
Appends a reversal and returns the stock.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Corrects a health record without rewriting history: appends a `reversal` record and one compensating stock `reversal` per medicine line (returning exactly what was used to the same location and lot). The withdrawal windows of the original stop counting.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Undo" a wrongly entered health record.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**

- Reversal record + compensating inventory movements; withdrawal windows end.
- A record can be reversed once (`409 record_already_reversed`); reversals cannot be reversed. To correct, reverse then POST a new record with `corrects_record_id` (same type and cycle).
- Stock movements created by health cannot be reversed through the inventory endpoint (`409 reverse_via_health_record`).
- This is a correction, not an edit: history is kept and a new opposite row is appended.

**IN THIS FLOW**

The expectation is derived from the chicken reference (21 days). Captures `breeding_project_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Starts an incubation (eggs) or pregnancy (females bred) attempt. The response carries a readable `reference` (`BRD-2026-00001`), the frozen `biological_reference`, and an `expectation` that is an exact date OR a window - never a midpoint.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Start breeding project" (incubation or pregnancy) on a livestock batch.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `breeding.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the project. No population, record or task is created (the API only recommends templates).
- A breeding project is ONE reproductive attempt on one livestock cycle (no individual animals or pedigrees). Eggs set and `expected_offspring` are estimates and never change population; only a recorded live outcome does.
- The expected date comes from the species' biological REFERENCE (a snapshot) or a manual entry. References are starting points, never guarantees.
- Closed cycles reject every write (`409 cycle_closed`); writes are rate limited (120/hour/user).

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Show a breeding project**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

**WHAT IT DOES**

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
A task is work that SHOULD happen. Captures `task_id`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Creates a one-off task (work that SHOULD happen), optionally tied to a cycle or breeding project, an assignee and a record type that will evidence it.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Add task" on the work screen or from a batch.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `task.manage` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the task only.
- A TASK is work that SHOULD happen. An operational record is what DID happen. A task never creates a record, a stock movement or a finance entry - not on creation, not when it becomes due, not on completion.
- `due_date` and `due_time` are farm-local (default `Africa/Lagos`); a task without a time is due by the end of its day. `due_state` is derived, never stored: `upcoming`, `due_today`, `overdue`, `completed`, `cancelled`.
- Writes are rate limited (240/hour/user).

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **List tasks**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

**IN THIS FLOW**
Completion only links the evidence; it creates nothing.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Closes the task, optionally linking an operational/health/breeding record that was ALREADY saved. Completion never creates that record.

**WHAT IT DOES**
A recurrence rule that GENERATES tasks: `daily` (every `interval_value` days), `weekly` (every `interval_value` weeks on `weekdays`, 1=Mon ... 7=Sun) or `none` (one task). Tasks are generated for today through the next 30 days and topped up daily by the scheduler.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Repeat" / recurring task setup.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**

- Creates the schedule and its first tasks.
- `due_date` and `due_time` are farm-local (default `Africa/Lagos`); a task without a time is due by the end of its day. `due_state` is derived, never stored: `upcoming`, `due_today`, `overdue`, `completed`, `cancelled`.
- Writes are rate limited (240/hour/user).
- Optional `ends_on` and/or `occurrence_limit`. Dates in the past are never generated. Nothing is generated while the cycle is closed or the project inactive.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
2 bags + 5 kg of feed (55 kg) and a delivery line: ONE stock-in and ONE expense of 10,250.45.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Records ONE procurement event: a supplier, a total and its lines. It is the only endpoint that writes stock AND money together, in a single transaction.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Record purchase" for stock bought from a supplier.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `recorded_at` = when it really happened (UTC, no milliseconds); `idempotency_key` = one UUID per user action.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `purchase.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the purchase and lines, one `stock_in` movement per stock line, and one linked expense in the money ledger (`source: purchase`).
- `stock` lines add stock (one `stock_in`, reason `purchase`, per line) using the Phase 5 components format; packages (`bag`) resolve ONLY through the item's own package conversion. `non_stock` lines (transport, services) move no stock.
- The purchase total is the exact sum of line `amount`s (`9000.00 + 1250.45 = 10250.45`); one expense is booked for the total unless `record_expense: false`. Its category is derived from the lines unless `finance_category_id` (an expense category) is sent.
- `production_cycle_id` (an OPEN cycle) allocates the cost to that cycle's profitability.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Show a purchase with its lines**.

**OUTPUT-NAMED STOCK LINES (GAP-08)**
A stock line names its stock with EXACTLY ONE of `inventory_item_id` (a specific item, always supported) or `output` (`eggs` | `milk`, the farm's automatic output item; no item id needed). A PURCHASE resolves (or creates) the output item exactly like `POST /inventory/stock-in {output}`, and with no store and no active store creates "Main Store". `storage_location_id` is optional with `output` (the only active store is used; several active stores need a choice, `422 items.N.storage_location_id`). Both or neither -> `422`; `output` on a non-stock line -> `422`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Unit codes come from `GET /master/units?dimension=...`; do not hard-code them.
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Derived numbers (population, stock, outstanding, totals) are authoritative on the server: refetch the affected resource and the dashboard after saving.
- Refetch inventory (`GET /inventory/items/{id}`) and finance summary after saving.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **15 — Contacts & Purchasing** -> "Record a purchase (stock + expense)".

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
90 eggs + 12 spent layers = 87,000.00. Stock-out and population exit happen NOW; no invoice and no income.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Records what LEFT the farm, to whom and for how much. A sale is the commercial event only: it is NOT an invoice and NOT a payment, so it books no income.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Record sale" (produce and/or animals).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- `recorded_at` = when it really happened (UTC, no milliseconds); `idempotency_key` = one UUID per user action.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `sale.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Sale + lines; one `stock_out` per stock line; one population exit (operational record `livestock_sale`, `population_delta = -12`) per livestock line. NO invoice, NO income.
- `stock` lines sell PRODUCE items: one stock-out (`reason: sale`) per line, quantities in the components format, never below zero (`409 insufficient_stock`, `details.available/requested`). `livestock` lines remove `head_count` animals from a livestock cycle through the population ledger (`409 insufficient_population`; cycle must be open). `other` lines (description required) have no physical effect.
- Customer: `contact_id` must be an active contact with the `customer` role, or send `customer_name` for a walk-in (not both).
- `finance_category_id` (an income category) is optional; otherwise derived (livestock-only -> `livestock_sales`, produce-only -> `crop_sales`, else `other_income`) and used when payments are booked.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Show a sale with its lines**.

**OUTPUT-NAMED STOCK LINES (GAP-08)**
A stock line names its stock with EXACTLY ONE of `inventory_item_id` (a specific item, always supported) or `output` (`eggs` | `milk`, the farm's automatic output item; no item id needed). A SALE takes the existing output item only: a farm that never stocked it gets `409 insufficient_stock` and nothing is created. `storage_location_id` is optional with `output` (the only active store is used; several active stores need a choice, `422 items.N.storage_location_id`). Both or neither -> `422`; `output` on a non-stock line -> `422`.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Unit codes come from `GET /master/units?dimension=...`; do not hard-code them.

**IN THIS FLOW**

**WHAT IT DOES**
Creates the customer DOCUMENT for a sale. The invoice snapshots the customer, seller, currency, total and every line when issued, so later edits to contacts or items never change it. It books nothing.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Create invoice" on a sale.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**

- One live invoice per sale: `409 invoice_exists`. A cancelled sale cannot be invoiced (`409 sale_cancelled`). `issue_date` defaults to today (between the sale day and today); `due_date` >= issue date.
- Void an invoice with `POST /invoices/{id}/void`; the sale can then be invoiced again.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
First instalment 30,000.00: THIS is when income is booked.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Records MONEY RECEIVED against an invoice. This is the moment income is booked (cash basis): one payment appends exactly one income row to the money ledger (`source: payment`).

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Record payment" on an invoice (partial or full).

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- Path ids (UUIDv7): `{{invoice_id}}`.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `payment.create` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates the payment and ONE income ledger row. Sale and invoice are unchanged except their derived `payment_status`/balance.
- `method`: `cash`, `bank_transfer`, `pos`, `mobile_money`, `cheque`, `other`. `received_on` is a farm-local day (not in the future, not before the sale).
- Partial and multiple payments are normal. A payment can never exceed the balance: `409 payment_exceeds_balance` (`details.outstanding`). A void invoice accepts none (`409 invoice_void`).
- Income uses the sale's category unless `finance_category_id` (an income category) is sent, and is allocated to a cycle only when all sale lines belong to ONE open cycle.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Record the final payment**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Route by the UUIDv7 `id`; any `reference` code (`BAT-2026-00001`, ...) is display-only.
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Derived numbers (population, stock, outstanding, totals) are authoritative on the server: refetch the affected resource and the dashboard after saving.
- Refetch the invoice and sale after paying; do not compute balances client-side.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
Needs the `data_export` plan feature. The job runs on the database queue: locally run `php artisan queue:work --once` (or use `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync`).

**WHAT IT DOES**
Queues a CSV, XLSX or PDF export of a report. The work runs on the database queue, so the response is `202` with `status: "queued"`; poll the export (or watch for the `export_ready` / `export_failed` notification) and download when `completed`.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Export" button on a report.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `report.export` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates an export row and queues a job that writes a private file (retained 7 days).
- Omitted dates are defaulted when the request is made and the RESOLVED filters are stored and echoed back, so the file always matches the request.
- `idempotency_key` (8-80 chars) is required and unique per user and farm: the same key + same content returns the SAME export (`200`, "Export already requested."); the same key with a different report, format or filters is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **Get an export (status)**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Do not poll tightly: back off (e.g. 2s, 5s, 10s) or use the notification.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **19 — Reports & Exports** -> "Request a report export".

PREREQUISITES: Flow 11 (an export produces an `export_ready` notification) and the scheduler/queue commands noted in the first request.

Notifications are generated by the scheduler: locally run `php artisan notifications:generate` first (and `php artisan queue:work --once` if the queue is not sync). Query booleans must be `1`/`0`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
The caller's in-app notifications for the current farm, newest first. `meta.unread_count` is the total unread count (use it for the bell badge).

The notification bell/center.

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Notifications are created by a background job (`notifications:generate`, hourly) - never by an API call. They follow three separate steps: condition -> decision (permission, preference, dedupe) -> record. They point at their source and never change it.
- Deduplication: critical/warning once per farm-local day, info once per week per user while the condition persists; one `export_ready` per export.
- Query: `unread` (`1`/`0`; the strings true/false are rejected here), `type`, `severity`, `page`, `per_page`.

- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.

request.description:
**IN THIS FLOW**
PREREQUISITES: Flow 1 and a farm plan that allows more than 3 team members (Flow S).

The invitation token only exists in the email. Locally copy it from `storage/logs/laravel.log` into `invitation_token`.

**WHAT IT DOES**
Invites someone to the farm with a preset role. The invitee receives an email with `{FRONTEND_URL}/invitations/accept?token=...` (valid 7 days, single use). The token is never returned by the API.

**WHEN TO USE IT**
"Invite team member" dialog.

**IMPORTANT INPUTS**
- None (no body or query parameters are required).

**IMPORTANT BEHAVIOR**
- Requires the farm permission `team.invite` (taken from the current farm context; never sent by the client).
- Creates a pending invitation and sends the invitation email (local: `storage/logs/laravel.log`).
- `role` is one of `manager`, `farm_worker`, `finance`, `vet` for an Owner; a Manager may only invite `farm_worker`, `finance`, `vet`. Nobody can invite or assign `owner` (`422 ownership_transfer_unsupported`).
- Pending invitations count toward the plan's `team_members` limit together with active members: when the limit is reached the call is `409 plan_limit_reached` (see `details`).
- Inviting someone who is already a member is `409 already_member`; a second open invitation to the same email is `409 invitation_already_pending`.

**WHAT TO DO NEXT**
Usual next request in the flow: **List open invitations**.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).
- Permissions come from the current farm context (`GET /farm` → `membership.permissions`); optional `X-Farm-Id` selects another farm you belong to.
- Fetch `GET /roles` to build the role picker: it says which roles the caller may assign. The invitation token only exists in the email, so locally copy it from `storage/logs/laravel.log` into the `invitation_token` environment variable.

Full reference (errors, all fields): folder **03 — Farms, Team & Access** -> "Invite a team member".

The invitee registers with the SAME email as the invitation.

**WHAT IT DOES**

**FARM DISCOVERY (GAP-07)**
`data.farms` lists every farm the user ACTIVELY belongs to (`id`, `name`, `role`; oldest membership first). `data.farm` stays the default farm (the oldest active membership). To work in another farm send its `farms[].id` as the `X-Farm-Id` header, then refetch `GET /farm` (membership + permissions) and `GET /subscription/entitlements` and clear farm-scoped caches. There is no switch endpoint. Permissions are never listed here.

**MARKETPLACE-ONLY SELLERS (Phase 22)**
`data.marketplace.shop_count` = Marketplace shops the user belongs to (any status). `next_action = "marketplace"` is returned only for a verified user with NO active farm who belongs to at least one shop: route to the seller dashboard (`GET /marketplace/my/shops`). A brand-new account with no shop still gets `complete_farm_setup` (offer "open a shop instead" -> `POST /marketplace/shops`, no farm needed). A user with a farm keeps `none`. Farm endpoints still answer `403 onboarding_required` / `no_active_farm`; `POST /onboarding/farm` remains available.

**FRONTEND NOTES**
- Cookie session + CSRF: send `X-XSRF-TOKEN` and a stateful `Origin` (the collection script does it; call `GET /auth/csrf-cookie` first).

Everyone.
